<path>docs/ARCHITECTURE.md</path>
<content>
1: # Architecture
2: 
3: ReqFlow is a **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron), not a web app.
4: Background and alternatives: [decisions/0002-electron-desktop-app.md](decisions/0002-electron-desktop-app.md).
5: Why the flow is built from blocks: [decisions/0003-building-blocks.md](decisions/0003-building-blocks.md).
6: 
7: ## Stack
8: 
9: | Concern         | Choice                                                                                | Why                                                                 |
10: | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
11: | Language        | TypeScript everywhere (npm workspaces)                                                | One shared contract for UI, engine and blocks                       |
12: | App shell       | Electron 44 (pinned, Node 24 inside), electron-vite 5, electron-builder               | Same Chromium on every OS; Node in the main process runs the engine |
13: | UI              | React 19 + React Router (hash routing) + Tailwind 4 + zustand 5                       | Renders from `file://` in the installed app; small, testable stores |
14: | Workflow canvas | `@xyflow/react` (React Flow 12)                                                       | The standard n8n-style node editor                                  |
15: | Schemas         | Zod 4                                                                                 | Runtime validation and TS types from one source                     |
16: | LLM             | Claude API (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`) behind `LlmClient`, plus a `mock` provider           | Swappable; works offline and in tests                               |
17: | Persistence     | SQLite via built-in `node:sqlite`, in the OS app-data folder                          | Zero setup, no native module to rebuild per OS                      |
18: | Tests           | Vitest (colocated `*.test.ts`) + `npm run smoke` (clicks through the app in Electron) | Fast unit tests; a real-app check without clicking                  |
19: 
20: ## Repo layout
21: 
22: ```
23: .
24: ├── AGENTS.md  PRODUCT.md  README.md   ← start here
25: ├── context/                           ← original hackathon briefing + the app sketch (read-only)
26: ├── docs/                              ← ARCHITECTURE, WORKSTREAMS, STATUS, decisions/ (ADRs)
27: ├── data/
28: │   ├── raw/        (gitignored)       ← BMW-provided datasets
29: │   └── samples/                       ← small synthetic datasets for dev
30: ├── packages/
31: │   ├── core/       ← CONTRACT: domain schemas, blocks.ts (block specs), graph.ts (graph rules), IPC API, fixtures
32: │   ├── engine/     ← block contract + registry (done); executor (WS1)
33: │   ├── blocks/     ← block implementations, one folder per block + default template
34: │   ├── llm/        ← LlmClient implementations: anthropic, mock (WS7)
35: │   └── db/         ← SQLite repositories, AuditLogger, FileStore (WS1)
36: └── apps/desktop/                      ← the Electron app
37:     ├── electron.vite.config.ts  electron-builder.yml  build/ (icons)
38:     └── src/
39:         ├── main/       ← Node: window, IPC handlers, wiring of engine/db/llm, smoke test
40:         ├── preload/    ← the bridge: allow-listed invoke + run-update events (keep tiny)
41:         └── renderer/src/
42:             ├── pages/        DataflowPage · CarPage · SettingsPage
43:             ├── components/   dataflow/ (editor + its store) · settings/ · shell/ (bottom tabs) · ui/ (shared controls)
44:             ├── lib/          api.ts (the only way to main) · settings.ts (settings store) · theme.ts
45:             └── router.tsx  globals.css (design tokens, light + dark)
46: ```
47: 
48: Dependency direction (no cycles): `core ← engine ← blocks`, `core ← llm`, `core ← db`, and
49: `apps/desktop/src/main` → all of them. The renderer imports only `@reqflow/core` (types, block specs,
50: graph rules, fixtures). It never imports engine, db, llm or blocks.
51: 
52: ## Processes and security
53: 
54: ```
55: renderer (React, sandboxed)  ──api.x.y(…)──▶  preload (allow-list)  ──IPC──▶  main (Node)
56:    no Node, no fs, no network                                              engine · SQLite · LLM · files · keychain
57:            ◀──────────────── runs.onUpdate(run) push events ────────────────────────┘
58: ```
59: 
60: - `contextIsolation`, `sandbox` and no `nodeIntegration`. Production builds get a strict CSP
61:   (`connect-src 'self'`): all network calls (Claude, web search) happen in main.
62: - The preload only forwards channels listed in `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS`. Main also checks that the sender is the app window.
63: - The window never navigates away. `http(s)` links open in the user's browser.
64: - API keys are entered in Settings, encrypted with Electron `safeStorage` (OS keychain) and never sent to
65:   the renderer. In dev, `apps/desktop/.env` is also read (see `.env.example`).
66: 
67: ## The building blocks (`packages/core/src/blocks.ts`)
68: 
69: A workflow is a tree of **workplaces**. Each workplace holds blocks and edges. Seven kinds of block
70: are in the palette, defined once in `BLOCK_SPECS` (label, description, group, params, ports, whether
71: it has an inner workplace):
72: 
73: | Block       | Ports                                 | Inner workplace | Params (placeholders for now)                 |
74: | ----------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
75: | Custom      | 1 in · 1 out                          | yes             | none                                          |
76: | Raw         | no input · 1 out (data stream)        | no              | Excel upload or database, dataset, file/query |
77: | Research    | no input · 1 out (same format as Raw) | yes             | question, source types, market, age, results  |
78: | AI Filter   | 1 in · 1 out (kept)                   | yes             | criterion, model, min. confidence             |
79: | AI Splitter | 1 in · one out **per branch**         | no              | split by, branches (list → ports), model      |
80: | HIL         | 1 in · 1 out                          | no              | reviewer, instructions, approvals, edits      |
81: | Add to Car  | one in **per ranking** · no output    | no              | rankings (list → ports), vehicle, market      |
82: 
83: - **Ports** come from `blockPorts(block)`. They can depend on params (the splitter's `branches`, Add to
84:   Car's `rankings`), and port ids are positional (`out-0`, `in-2`). When params change, `setBlockParams`
85:   removes edges on ports that no longer exist and returns them, so the editor can tell the user.
86: - **Params** are declared as `ParamSpec`s (text, textarea, number, slider, select, multiselect, toggle,
87:   list, file). The editor renders a form from them, and `parseBlockParams` validates strictly (unknown
88:   keys and wrong types are errors). Select options with the value `"global"` mean "use Settings →
89:   Global parameters".
90: - **Inner workplaces** (Custom, Research, AI Filter) hold a sub-flow built from the same blocks,
91:   recursively. Each one has fixed **boundary blocks**: one `block_input` per input port of the parent
92:   and one `block_output` per output port. They are created with the block and can't be deleted.
93: - **Ids** are unique across the whole tree, so run status and outputs are keyed by block id alone.
94: - **Graph rules** live in `packages/core/src/graph.ts` and are shared by the editor and the engine:
95:   `checkConnection` (ports exist, no self-loop, no duplicates, no cycles), `connect`, `removeBlocks`,
96:   `setBlockParams`, `graphAt` / `updateGraphAt` (navigate the tree), `validateGraph` (everything,
97:   recursively). Several edges may enter one input (merged) or leave one output (fan-out).
98: 
99: ## Data flow: one envelope per port
100: 
101: Every port carries a `PipelineData` envelope (`sources, records, findings, themes, requirements`).
102: Raw and Research emit sources and records (the "unified data stream"). Later blocks enrich the same
103: envelope: AI Filter keeps matching items (and extracts evidence-linked findings), AI Splitter routes
104: items to one branch each, HIL passes on what the reviewer approved, and Add to Car turns what arrives
105: into requirements; the input it arrives on sets the ranking. Several edges into one input are combined
106: with `mergePipelineData` (concatenate, de-duplicate by `id`, later edge wins).
107: 
108: ```ts
109: defineBlock({
110:   kind: "ai_filter",
111:   async run(inputs, params, ctx) {
112:     const input = inputs.in; // one envelope per input port id
113:     /* ctx.llm, ctx.audit, ctx.log … */
114:     return { status: "ok", outputs: { out: kept } }; // one envelope per output port id
115:   },
116: });
117: ```
118: 
119: ## Engine semantics (WS1 implements, everyone relies on)
120: 
121: 1. **Validate before running** with `validateGraph`, and check that every block kind (except
122:    Custom) has an implementation (`BlockRegistry.missing()`). If anything fails, the run fails before it
123:    starts, with per-block errors.
124: 2. **Execute each workplace in topological order.** A block's input per port is the merge of what its
125:    incoming edges carry. Store each block's output per port and push `BlockRun` status, counts, logs
126:    and progress via `runs.onUpdate`.
127: 3. **Inner workplaces.** A block whose inner workplace contains blocks runs that sub-flow: each
128:    `block_input` emits what arrived on its parent port, and what reaches each `block_output` becomes
129:    the parent's output on that port. A Custom block always runs its sub-flow. Research and AI Filter run
130:    their built-in implementation while their inner workplace is empty.
131: 4. **Failure.** A block that throws is marked `failed`, its downstream blocks `skipped`, and the run
132:    `failed`. Nothing is partially published.
133: 5. **Pause / resume.** HIL returns `{ status: "paused" }` → the run is `waiting_for_review`.
134:    `runs.resume` reloads what the reviewer changed, re-invokes the block with `ctx.resumed = true`, and continues.
135: 6. **Cancel.** The run's `AbortSignal` fires, and blocks must stop promptly.
136: 7. **Audit.** The engine logs `run.*` events, blocks log what they create or change, and handlers log human actions.
137: 
138: ## IPC API (`packages/core/src/ipc.ts`)
139: 
140: UI code calls `api.<namespace>.<method>(…)` from `@/lib/api`. Main implements `ReqflowHandlers`
141: (`apps/desktop/src/main/handlers.ts`). Failures arrive as `ReqflowError` with a `code`
142: (`invalid_input`, `not_found`, `not_implemented`, `internal`, …). Arguments must be plain data. Main
143: validates every argument with the Zod schemas, because the renderer counts as untrusted input.
144: 
145: | Method                                               | Purpose                                                                                                                                   |
146: | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
147: | `app.info()`                                         | Version, OS, data directory (**built**)                                                                                                   |
148: | `templates.list()`                                   | Workflow templates (`BMW_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE`) (**built**)                                                                                   |
149: | `workflows.list/get/save/remove`                     | Workflow CRUD. `save` assigns the id and bumps `version`                                                                                  |
150: | `blocks.preview(request)`                            | Runs a block without inputs (Raw) on its own and returns its output and log (**built**)                                                   |
151: | `files.import()`                                     | Native open dialog → copies the file into the data dir → `StoredFileInfo` (`null` if cancelled). Raw's `file` param stores it (**built**) |
152: | `runs.start/get/list/blockOutput/resume/cancel`      | Run lifecycle. `blockOutput` returns that block's output per port                                                                         |
153: | `runs.onUpdate(listener)`                            | Push events on every status, progress or log change (no polling)                                                                          |
154: | `requirements.list(filter)` · `requirements.get(id)` | Latest versions · `RequirementDetail` (findings, evidence, sources, versions)                                                             |
155: | `requirements.edit(id, RequirementEdit)`             | PM edit, rationale required → new version and audit                                                                                       |
156: | `requirements.decide(id, RequirementDecision)`       | Approve / reject / defer / challenge / reopen. A challenge makes the AI answer (`challenge_answered`) and returns it to `in_review`       |
157: | `requirements.reset()`                               | Removes every requirement (Car page → Reset). Writes one `requirement.deleted` audit event each; ids are never reused                     |
158: | `audit.list(filter)`                                 | Audit events, ascending by time                                                                                                           |
159: | `settings.get/save` · `settings.secrets/setSecret`   | `Settings` (save logs `settings.changed` with a diff) · API-key status / store a key in the keychain                                      |
160: | `exports.requirements({ runId, format })`            | Native save dialog → JSON / CSV / Markdown (logs `export.created`)                                                                        |
161: 
162: To add a method: add it to `ReqflowApi` **and** `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS` (the compiler enforces both),
163: then implement it in `handlers.ts`.
164: 
165: ## HIL review report
166: 
167: Double-clicking a HIL block (or its report icon) opens `components/dataflow/report/HilReport.tsx`:
168: 
169: - **Flow chart** from `traceLineage(root, path, blockId)` (`packages/core/src/lineage.ts`): every step
170:   data passes through on its way into the block. It leaves inner workplaces through their
171:   `block_input` and traces through the sub-flow of upstream blocks that have blocks inside.
172: - **Data at a step** (table icon on every step; the HIL itself = "data at this point"). Steps without
173:   inputs (Raw) show their **real data** via `blocks.preview`, and so does a HIL fed directly by them.
174:   After a run it shows `api.runs.blockOutput()` of the step (for the HIL: the merge of what its
175:   incoming edges carried). Otherwise it says nothing has arrived yet; there is no demo data.
176: - At run time the HIL block (`packages/blocks/src/hil/hil.ts`) pauses the run until the review is done
177:   and then passes the data on unchanged; edits go through the requirement API (audited).
178: 
179: ## Renderer state
180: 
181: - **`components/dataflow/store.ts`**: the editor store (zustand). It holds the workflow tree, the
182:   open workplace (`path`), the selection, React Flow sizes and a notice. Every edit goes through the
183:   core graph rules; errors become a visible notice, never a silent no-op. It lives for the whole app
184:   session, so switching tabs keeps the flow. It isn't saved to disk yet (`workflows.*` is WS1).
185: - **`lib/settings.ts`**: the settings store. It loads `settings.get()` at startup, validates every
186:   change with the `Settings` schema and saves in the background. While main has no settings storage
187:   (`not_implemented`), it keeps the defaults and the Settings page says so.
188: - **zustand 5 rule:** never return a new object or array from a selector (it re-renders forever).
189:   Select existing objects or primitives and derive the rest with `useMemo`.
190: - **Theme:** `lib/theme.ts` sets `<html data-theme>` from Settings (system, light or dark). The CSS
191:   tokens in `globals.css` follow it, so use token classes (`bg-panel`, `text-muted`, …), never hex colors.
192: - **Colorway: BMW M.** The M stripe colours (`m-light` #81C4FF, `m-dark` #16588E, `m-red` #E7222E) on
193:   carbon neutrals. Block groups take them: sources light blue, AI dark blue, HIL red (a person has to
194:   act), Add to Car neutral. `MStripe` (`components/ui/`) marks the active tab. Filled controls use
195:   `bg-brand-fill` so white text stays readable in both themes.
196: 
197: ## AI usage rules
198: 
199: - Use `ctx.llm.generateObject` with a Zod schema for every AI step. Invalid output → throw.
200: - **Never trust model-cited evidence.** The model returns `recordId` and `excerpt`. Code checks that
201:   the excerpt is a verbatim substring of that record, and drops or flags the finding if it isn't.
202: - Batch the records. Use `tier: "fast"` for per-record extraction and `default` for clustering, derivation and challenges.
203: - AI actors in the audit trail record the exact model id returned by the client.
204: - The `mock` provider must return schema-valid, deterministic output so the whole pipeline runs offline.
205: - Prompts live next to the block that uses them (`blocks/src/<block>/<name>.prompt.ts`).
206: 
207: ## Persistence notes (WS1)
208: 
209: - The database lives in the per-user app-data folder (`main/paths.ts`: macOS
210:   `~/Library/Application Support/ReqFlow/data`, Windows `%APPDATA%\ReqFlow\data`, Linux
211:   `~/.config/ReqFlow/data`). `REQFLOW_DATA_DIR` overrides it. Always build paths with `node:path`, never
212:   with string concatenation (Windows uses `\`).
213: - Only one app instance runs at a time (single-instance lock), so only one process writes SQLite.
214: - Workflows are stored whole (the block tree as JSON) and versioned on save.
215: - Requirements are versioned: one row per `(id, version)`. "Current" means the max version.
216: - `audit_events` is insert-only, with no update or delete code path.
217: - Block outputs are stored per `(runId, blockId, port)` as JSON. Imported files are copied into `uploads/`
218:   inside the data dir by the file store (`packages/db/src/files.ts`, built), metadata next to each file.
219: 
220: ## Running, checking, packaging
221: 
222: | Command (repo root) | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
223: | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
224: | `npm run dev`       | Opens the app with hot reload (renderer) and auto-restart (main)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
225: | `npm run smoke`     | Builds, then drives the real app off screen: opens every screen, adds every block, opens an inner workplace, types into fields, connects ports by mouse drag (and checks a loop is refused), walks the settings, switches to dark mode, screenshots each step to `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`, checks the IPC bridge, and exits non-zero on any failed check or renderer error |
226: | `npm run check`     | Typecheck + unit tests + format check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
227: | `npm run package`   | Installer for the **current** OS in `apps/desktop/release/`: `.exe` (NSIS), `.dmg` or `.AppImage`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
228: 
229: Installers must be built on their own OS (or in a CI matrix later). Builds are unsigned, so macOS
230: Gatekeeper and Windows SmartScreen show a warning on first launch. Code signing is out of scope for the
231: hackathon. Linux CI needs a virtual display (`xvfb-run`) for `smoke`.
</content>

# Architecture

ReqFlow is a **native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron), not a web app.
Background and alternatives: [decisions/0002-electron-desktop-app.md](decisions/0002-electron-desktop-app.md).
Why the flow is built from blocks: [decisions/0003-building-blocks.md](decisions/0003-building-blocks.md).

## Stack

| Concern         | Choice                                                                                | Why                                                                 |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Language        | TypeScript everywhere (npm workspaces)                                                | One shared contract for UI, engine and blocks                       |
| App shell       | Electron 44 (pinned, Node 24 inside), electron-vite 5, electron-builder               | Same Chromium on every OS; Node in the main process runs the engine |
| UI              | React 19 + React Router (hash routing) + Tailwind 4 + zustand 5                       | Renders from `file://` in the installed app; small, testable stores |
| Workflow canvas | `@xyflow/react` (React Flow 12)                                                       | The standard n8n-style node editor                                  |
| Schemas         | Zod 4                                                                                 | Runtime validation and TS types from one source                     |
| LLM             | Claude API (`@anthropic-ai/sdk`) behind `LlmClient`, plus a `mock` provider           | Swappable; works offline and in tests                               |
| Persistence     | SQLite via built-in `node:sqlite`, in the OS app-data folder                          | Zero setup, no native module to rebuild per OS                      |
| Tests           | Vitest (colocated `*.test.ts`) + `npm run smoke` (clicks through the app in Electron) | Fast unit tests; a real-app check without clicking                  |

## Repo layout

```
.
├── AGENTS.md  PRODUCT.md  README.md   ← start here
├── context/                           ← original hackathon briefing + the app sketch (read-only)
├── docs/                              ← ARCHITECTURE, WORKSTREAMS, STATUS, decisions/ (ADRs)
├── data/
│   ├── raw/        (gitignored)       ← BMW-provided datasets
│   └── samples/                       ← small synthetic datasets for dev
├── packages/
│   ├── core/       ← CONTRACT: domain schemas, blocks.ts (block specs), graph.ts (graph rules), IPC API, fixtures
│   ├── engine/     ← block contract + registry (done); executor (WS1)
│   ├── blocks/     ← block implementations, one folder per block + default template
│   ├── llm/        ← LlmClient implementations: anthropic, mock (WS7)
│   └── db/         ← SQLite repositories, AuditLogger, FileStore (WS1)
└── apps/desktop/                      ← the Electron app
    ├── electron.vite.config.ts  electron-builder.yml  build/ (icons)
    └── src/
        ├── main/       ← Node: window, IPC handlers, wiring of engine/db/llm, smoke test
        ├── preload/    ← the bridge: allow-listed invoke + run-update events (keep tiny)
        └── renderer/src/
            ├── pages/        DataflowPage · CarPage · SettingsPage
            ├── components/   dataflow/ (editor + its store) · settings/ · shell/ (bottom tabs) · ui/ (shared controls)
            ├── lib/          api.ts (the only way to main) · settings.ts (settings store) · theme.ts
            └── router.tsx  globals.css (design tokens, light + dark)
```

Dependency direction (no cycles): `core ← engine ← blocks`, `core ← llm`, `core ← db`, and
`apps/desktop/src/main` → all of them. The renderer imports only `@reqflow/core` (types, block specs,
graph rules, fixtures). It never imports engine, db, llm or blocks.

## Processes and security

```
renderer (React, sandboxed)  ──api.x.y(…)──▶  preload (allow-list)  ──IPC──▶  main (Node)
   no Node, no fs, no network                                              engine · SQLite · LLM · files · keychain
           ◀──────────────── runs.onUpdate(run) push events ────────────────────────┘
```

- `contextIsolation`, `sandbox` and no `nodeIntegration`. Production builds get a strict CSP
  (`connect-src 'self'`): all network calls (Claude, web search) happen in main.
- The preload only forwards channels listed in `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS`. Main also checks that the sender is the app window.
- The window never navigates away. `http(s)` links open in the user's browser.
- API keys are entered in Settings, encrypted with Electron `safeStorage` (OS keychain) and never sent to
  the renderer. In dev, `apps/desktop/.env` is also read (see `.env.example`).

## The building blocks (`packages/core/src/blocks.ts`)

A workflow is a tree of **workplaces**. Each workplace holds blocks and edges. Seven kinds of block
are in the palette, defined once in `BLOCK_SPECS` (label, description, group, params, ports, whether
it has an inner workplace):

| Block       | Ports                                 | Inner workplace | Params (placeholders for now)                 |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Custom      | 1 in · 1 out                          | yes             | none                                          |
| Raw         | no input · 1 out (data stream)        | no              | Excel upload or database, dataset, file/query |
| Research    | no input · 1 out (same format as Raw) | yes             | question, source types, market, age, results  |
| AI Filter   | 1 in · 1 out (kept)                   | yes             | criterion, model, min. confidence             |
| AI Splitter | 1 in · one out **per branch**         | no              | split by, branches (list → ports), model      |
| HIL         | 1 in · 1 out                          | no              | reviewer, instructions, approvals, edits      |
| Add to Car  | one in **per ranking** · no output    | no              | rankings (list → ports), vehicle, market      |

- **Ports** come from `blockPorts(block)`. They can depend on params (the splitter's `branches`, Add to
  Car's `rankings`), and port ids are positional (`out-0`, `in-2`). When params change, `setBlockParams`
  removes edges on ports that no longer exist and returns them, so the editor can tell the user.
- **Params** are declared as `ParamSpec`s (text, textarea, number, slider, select, multiselect, toggle,
  list, file). The editor renders a form from them, and `parseBlockParams` validates strictly (unknown
  keys and wrong types are errors). Select options with the value `"global"` mean "use Settings →
  Global parameters".
- **Inner workplaces** (Custom, Research, AI Filter) hold a sub-flow built from the same blocks,
  recursively. Each one has fixed **boundary blocks**: one `block_input` per input port of the parent
  and one `block_output` per output port. They are created with the block and can't be deleted.
- **Ids** are unique across the whole tree, so run status and outputs are keyed by block id alone.
- **Graph rules** live in `packages/core/src/graph.ts` and are shared by the editor and the engine:
  `checkConnection` (ports exist, no self-loop, no duplicates, no cycles), `connect`, `removeBlocks`,
  `setBlockParams`, `graphAt` / `updateGraphAt` (navigate the tree), `validateGraph` (everything,
  recursively). Several edges may enter one input (merged) or leave one output (fan-out).

## Data flow: one envelope per port

Every port carries a `PipelineData` envelope (`sources, records, findings, themes, requirements`).
Raw and Research emit sources and records (the "unified data stream"). Later blocks enrich the same
envelope: AI Filter keeps matching items (and extracts evidence-linked findings), AI Splitter routes
items to one branch each, HIL passes on what the reviewer approved, and Add to Car turns what arrives
into requirements; the input it arrives on sets the ranking. Several edges into one input are combined
with `mergePipelineData` (concatenate, de-duplicate by `id`, later edge wins).

```ts
defineBlock({
  kind: "ai_filter",
  async run(inputs, params, ctx) {
    const input = inputs.in; // one envelope per input port id
    /* ctx.llm, ctx.audit, ctx.log … */
    return { status: "ok", outputs: { out: kept } }; // one envelope per output port id
  },
});
```

## Engine semantics (WS1 implements, everyone relies on)

1. **Validate before running** with `validateGraph`, and check that every block kind (except
   Custom) has an implementation (`BlockRegistry.missing()`). If anything fails, the run fails before it
   starts, with per-block errors.
2. **Execute each workplace in topological order.** A block's input per port is the merge of what its
   incoming edges carry. Store each block's output per port and push `BlockRun` status, counts, logs
   and progress via `runs.onUpdate`.
3. **Inner workplaces.** A block whose inner workplace contains blocks runs that sub-flow: each
   `block_input` emits what arrived on its parent port, and what reaches each `block_output` becomes
   the parent's output on that port. A Custom block always runs its sub-flow. Research and AI Filter run
   their built-in implementation while their inner workplace is empty.
4. **Failure.** A block that throws is marked `failed`, its downstream blocks `skipped`, and the run
   `failed`. Nothing is partially published.
5. **Pause / resume.** HIL returns `{ status: "paused" }` → the run is `waiting_for_review`.
   `runs.resume` reloads what the reviewer changed, re-invokes the block with `ctx.resumed = true`, and continues.
6. **Cancel.** The run's `AbortSignal` fires, and blocks must stop promptly.
7. **Audit.** The engine logs `run.*` events, blocks log what they create or change, and handlers log human actions.

## IPC API (`packages/core/src/ipc.ts`)

UI code calls `api.<namespace>.<method>(…)` from `@/lib/api`. Main implements `ReqflowHandlers`
(`apps/desktop/src/main/handlers.ts`). Failures arrive as `ReqflowError` with a `code`
(`invalid_input`, `not_found`, `not_implemented`, `internal`, …). Arguments must be plain data. Main
validates every argument with the Zod schemas, because the renderer counts as untrusted input.

| Method                                               | Purpose                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app.info()`                                         | Version, OS, data directory (**built**)                                                                                                   |
| `templates.list()`                                   | Workflow templates (`BMW_DEFAULT_TEMPLATE`) (**built**)                                                                                   |
| `workflows.list/get/save/remove`                     | Workflow CRUD. `save` assigns the id and bumps `version`                                                                                  |
| `blocks.preview(request)`                            | Runs a block without inputs (Raw) on its own and returns its output and log (**built**)                                                   |
| `files.import()`                                     | Native open dialog → copies the file into the data dir → `StoredFileInfo` (`null` if cancelled). Raw's `file` param stores it (**built**) |
| `runs.start/get/list/blockOutput/resume/cancel`      | Run lifecycle. `blockOutput` returns that block's output per port                                                                         |
| `runs.onUpdate(listener)`                            | Push events on every status, progress or log change (no polling)                                                                          |
| `requirements.list(filter)` · `requirements.get(id)` | Latest versions · `RequirementDetail` (findings, evidence, sources, versions)                                                             |
| `requirements.edit(id, RequirementEdit)`             | PM edit, rationale required → new version and audit                                                                                       |
| `requirements.decide(id, RequirementDecision)`       | Approve / reject / defer / challenge / reopen. A challenge makes the AI answer (`challenge_answered`) and returns it to `in_review`       |
| `requirements.reset()`                               | Removes every requirement (Car page → Reset). Writes one `requirement.deleted` audit event each; ids are never reused                     |
| `audit.list(filter)`                                 | Audit events, ascending by time                                                                                                           |
| `settings.get/save` · `settings.secrets/setSecret`   | `Settings` (save logs `settings.changed` with a diff) · API-key status / store a key in the keychain                                      |
| `exports.requirements({ runId, format })`            | Native save dialog → JSON / CSV / Markdown (logs `export.created`)                                                                        |

To add a method: add it to `ReqflowApi` **and** `IPC_INVOKE_METHODS` (the compiler enforces both),
then implement it in `handlers.ts`.

## HIL review report

Double-clicking a HIL block (or its report icon) opens `components/dataflow/report/HilReport.tsx`:

- **Flow chart** from `traceLineage(root, path, blockId)` (`packages/core/src/lineage.ts`): every step
  data passes through on its way into the block. It leaves inner workplaces through their
  `block_input` and traces through the sub-flow of upstream blocks that have blocks inside.
- **Data at a step** (table icon on every step; the HIL itself = "data at this point"). Steps without
  inputs (Raw) show their **real data** via `blocks.preview`, and so does a HIL fed directly by them.
  After a run it shows `api.runs.blockOutput()` of the step (for the HIL: the merge of what its
  incoming edges carried). Otherwise it says nothing has arrived yet; there is no demo data.
- At run time the HIL block (`packages/blocks/src/hil/hil.ts`) pauses the run until the review is done
  and then passes the data on unchanged; edits go through the requirement API (audited).

## Renderer state

- **`components/dataflow/store.ts`**: the editor store (zustand). It holds the workflow tree, the
  open workplace (`path`), the selection, React Flow sizes and a notice. Every edit goes through the
  core graph rules; errors become a visible notice, never a silent no-op. It lives for the whole app
  session, so switching tabs keeps the flow. It isn't saved to disk yet (`workflows.*` is WS1).
- **`lib/settings.ts`**: the settings store. It loads `settings.get()` at startup, validates every
  change with the `Settings` schema and saves in the background. While main has no settings storage
  (`not_implemented`), it keeps the defaults and the Settings page says so.
- **zustand 5 rule:** never return a new object or array from a selector (it re-renders forever).
  Select existing objects or primitives and derive the rest with `useMemo`.
- **Theme:** `lib/theme.ts` sets `<html data-theme>` from Settings (system, light or dark). The CSS
  tokens in `globals.css` follow it, so use token classes (`bg-panel`, `text-muted`, …), never hex colors.
- **Colorway: BMW M.** The M stripe colours (`m-light` #81C4FF, `m-dark` #16588E, `m-red` #E7222E) on
  carbon neutrals. Block groups take them: sources light blue, AI dark blue, HIL red (a person has to
  act), Add to Car neutral. `MStripe` (`components/ui/`) marks the active tab. Filled controls use
  `bg-brand-fill` so white text stays readable in both themes.

## AI usage rules

- Use `ctx.llm.generateObject` with a Zod schema for every AI step. Invalid output → throw.
- **Never trust model-cited evidence.** The model returns `recordId` and `excerpt`. Code checks that
  the excerpt is a verbatim substring of that record, and drops or flags the finding if it isn't.
- Batch the records. Use `tier: "fast"` for per-record extraction and `default` for clustering, derivation and challenges.
- AI actors in the audit trail record the exact model id returned by the client.
- The `mock` provider must return schema-valid, deterministic output so the whole pipeline runs offline.
- Prompts live next to the block that uses them (`blocks/src/<block>/<name>.prompt.ts`).

## Persistence notes (WS1)

- The database lives in the per-user app-data folder (`main/paths.ts`: macOS
  `~/Library/Application Support/ReqFlow/data`, Windows `%APPDATA%\ReqFlow\data`, Linux
  `~/.config/ReqFlow/data`). `REQFLOW_DATA_DIR` overrides it. Always build paths with `node:path`, never
  with string concatenation (Windows uses `\`).
- Only one app instance runs at a time (single-instance lock), so only one process writes SQLite.
- Workflows are stored whole (the block tree as JSON) and versioned on save.
- Requirements are versioned: one row per `(id, version)`. "Current" means the max version.
- `audit_events` is insert-only, with no update or delete code path.
- Block outputs are stored per `(runId, blockId, port)` as JSON. Imported files are copied into `uploads/`
  inside the data dir by the file store (`packages/db/src/files.ts`, built), metadata next to each file.

## Running, checking, packaging

| Command (repo root) | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run dev`       | Opens the app with hot reload (renderer) and auto-restart (main)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `npm run smoke`     | Builds, then drives the real app off screen: opens every screen, adds every block, opens an inner workplace, types into fields, connects ports by mouse drag (and checks a loop is refused), walks the settings, switches to dark mode, screenshots each step to `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`, checks the IPC bridge, and exits non-zero on any failed check or renderer error |
| `npm run check`     | Typecheck + unit tests + format check                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `npm run package`   | Installer for the **current** OS in `apps/desktop/release/`: `.exe` (NSIS), `.dmg` or `.AppImage`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

Installers must be built on their own OS (or in a CI matrix later). Builds are unsigned, so macOS
Gatekeeper and Windows SmartScreen show a warning on first launch. Code signing is out of scope for the
hackathon. Linux CI needs a virtual display (`xvfb-run`) for `smoke`.

# Workstreams — how to split the work across agents

Each workstream (WS) owns a set of paths, so parallel agents never edit the same files. Everything
builds against the contract in `packages/core` (block specs in `blocks.ts`, graph rules in `graph.ts`)
and the block contract in `packages/engine/src/block.ts`. UI workstreams use `@reqflow/core/fixtures`
until the API is live. Block workstreams test with fixtures and the `mock` LLM.

## Starting an agent

Paste [AGENT_PROMPT.md](AGENT_PROMPT.md) into the agent, with the workstream filled in. Agents claim
work and hand it off in [STATUS.md](STATUS.md), each editing only its own section. **The concrete,
ordered task list for every workstream lives in STATUS.md**; this file defines scope, file ownership
and "done when".

## UI agents (WS2–WS4)

The renderer is sandboxed: no Node, no `fs`, no `fetch` to the internet. Reach data only through
`api` from `@/lib/api`. Until WS1 implements a method, it throws `ReqflowError` with code
`not_implemented`. Show that state, or render `@reqflow/core/fixtures` meanwhile. Reuse the shared
controls in `components/ui/` and the design tokens in `globals.css` (light and dark). Check your
screens with `npm run smoke` (screenshots land in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`), and extend
`apps/desktop/src/main/smoke.ts` (ask WS1/WS0) when you add an interaction worth guarding.

## Git

Use one branch per workstream (`ws1-engine`, `ws2-editor`, …), ideally in its own `git worktree`. Make small
commits (`ws<N>: …`), push right away, and rebase on `main` at least hourly. Merge into `main` through a PR
with a merge commit, never a squash, so Entire's checkpoint trailers survive. To add a dependency, add it to **your own** package's
`package.json` only. If `package-lock.json` conflicts, run `npm install` again.

## Phases

0. **Done (lead):** repo skeleton, the contract (`core`: schemas, block specs, graph rules), the block
   contract and registry, the default template, fixtures, the app shell with its three tabs, the Data
   Flow editor (structure), the Settings page and the Car placeholder.
1. **Parallel:** WS1–WS8 below.
2. **Integration (lead):** wire services and the registry in `apps/desktop/src/main`, run the default template end
   to end with `mock`, then with Claude and the real BMW data, then polish the demo.

---

### WS0 — Lead / integrator (main session)

**Owns:** `packages/core/**`, `docs/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, root config files.
**Does:** merges branches, reviews and applies contract changes (including block params and ports), runs
integration (phase 2) and keeps docs current.

### WS1 — Engine, persistence & main process

**Owns:** `packages/engine/**`, `packages/db/**`, `apps/desktop/src/main/**`, `apps/desktop/src/preload/**`,
`packages/blocks/src/hil/**`, `packages/blocks/src/index.ts`, `packages/blocks/src/templates/**`.
**Builds:**

- **First,** the handlers the UIs need: `settings.get/save` (the Settings page already calls them),
  `workflows.*` (so the editor can save and load), `files.import` (Raw's file param), and read-only
  `requirements.*` / `audit.list` serving the core fixtures until the DB lands.
- The executor (see ARCHITECTURE.md → Engine semantics): `validateGraph`, topological run per workplace,
  inner workplaces via boundary blocks, merge per input port, per-port output storage, failure →
  skipped, pause/resume at HIL, cancel. Wire `BlockContext` (including `ctx.car.add` → DB).
- SQLite repositories, versioned requirements, append-only `AuditLogger`, `FileStore`, settings storage.
- Every method in `main/handlers.ts` (replace each `notBuilt`), with Zod validation of all arguments. Wire registry, LLM, web search, DB and keychain (`safeStorage`) in `main/`; push run updates via `IPC_EVENTS.runUpdate`.
- The HIL block (pause until reviewed, then pass on what the reviewer kept).

**Done when:** executor tests pass with fake blocks (success, failure, multi-port merge, splitter
fan-out, inner workplace, pause → resume, cancel). Every IPC method works against SQLite (none left
`not_implemented`). A run of fake blocks streams updates to `runs.onUpdate`.

### WS2 — Data Flow editor UI

**Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/DataflowPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/dataflow/**`.
**State today:** palette, workplace (React Flow), blocks with ports, connect with validation, inspector
with parameter forms, inner workplaces with breadcrumb, delete with confirmation, snap/minimap from
Settings. The flow lives in memory (`components/dataflow/store.ts`).
**Builds next:** save/load (`api.workflows.*`, autosave), "New from template" (`api.templates.list()`),
undo/redo, copy/paste, a Run button with live status, counts and logs on each block
(`api.runs.onUpdate()`), an output inspector (`api.runs.blockOutput()`), and a "waiting for review"
banner linking to the Car tab.
**Done when:** you can build the default template by hand, save it, reload it, and see run states on the
blocks (mocked until WS1 lands).

### WS3 — Car tab: requirements review & audit UI

**Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/CarPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/car/**`,
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/requirements/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/audit/**`.
**Builds:** the Car tab as the output page: the car (keep the car visual) with its requirements as a
list or board, grouped by ranking, with filters and sorting. A detail view shows targets, a score
breakdown (factor × weight with notes), priority and rationale, an evidence level badge, assumptions,
uncertainties and conflicting evidence, and a drill-down from findings to verbatim excerpts to sources.
Add a decision bar (approve / reject / defer / challenge) where rationale is required, inline editing
with rationale, a History view, a global audit timeline with before → after diffs and filters, a
resume-run action, and export.
**Done when:** every field from the briefing's deliverable list is visible for the fixture requirements,
and the decision and edit flows call `api.requirements.*`.

### WS4 — Settings, app shell & packaging

**Owns:** `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/settings/**`,
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/shell/**`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/components/ui/**` (shared controls),
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/settings*.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/lib/theme.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/router.tsx`,
`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/globals.css`, `apps/desktop/electron-builder.yml`, `apps/desktop/build/**` (app icons).
**State today:** bottom tab bar (⌘/Ctrl 1–3), Settings with App, Global parameters, AI & research,
Collaboration and About; theme switching (system/light/dark); every change validated with the
`Settings` schema. Not saved yet (waits for WS1's `settings.save`).
**Builds next:** API-key entry once `settings.setSecret` exists (never display a stored key), a
`settings.changed` audit entry once WS1 logs it, the app icon and installer config, demo polish.
**Done when:** settings load, validate, save and appear as a `settings.changed` audit event, the shell looks
demo-ready, and `npm run package` produces a working installer on your OS.

### WS5 — Raw block (BMW data ingestion)

**Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/raw/**`, `data/samples/**`.
**Builds:** the Raw block. Params (see `BLOCK_SPECS.raw`): Excel upload (`file` = `{ fileId, name }`
from `api.files.import()`, `sheet`) or database (`dbType`, `connection`, `query`; never store
passwords in params), plus `dataset`. It parses the provided formats (CSV, XLSX and whatever BMW
ships: check `data/raw/` once it arrives) into `Source` + `SourceRecord[]` with locators and language.
Structured datasets (equipment take rates, sales volumes) also emit deterministic `usage_pattern`
findings (for example a high take rate signals a basic expectation) with evidence. Also write
synthetic sample files in `data/samples/` that match the real formats. Param changes → request via WS0.
**Done when:** each sample dataset ingests in tests, errors name the bad row or column, and no data is dropped silently.

### WS6 — Research block

**Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/research/**`.
**Builds:** the Research block. It turns its params and the scope into queries (competitors in the
segment, owner and press reviews, market and technology trends for the horizon), runs them through
`ctx.web`, fetches pages and extracts clean text into `SourceRecord`s — the same stream format as Raw —
and sets the `Source` kind, publisher, date and **reliability** (with the rule documented). It respects
allowed and blocked domains and de-duplicates by URL. Also implement `WebSearch` providers
(`anthropic_web_search`, `tavily`) as factories that take keys as arguments (WS1 wires them).
**Done when:** a recorded or offline test run produces sources with working URLs and reliability, and failures are logged rather than swallowed.

### WS7 — AI blocks: AI Filter, AI Splitter, Add to Car

**Owns:** `packages/llm/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-filter/**`, `packages/blocks/src/ai-splitter/**`,
`packages/blocks/src/add-to-car/**`.
**Builds:** an `LlmClient` with a Claude provider and a deterministic `mock` provider (use the `claude-api`
skill for SDK details). **AI Filter**: keep items matching the criterion and extract evidence-linked
findings (verbatim-excerpt verification; out-of-scope items logged with a reason). **AI Splitter**:
route every item to exactly one branch (`out-<i>`); "Split by: Priority" uses WS8's scoring.
**Add to Car**: cluster and derive customer-facing, actionable requirements (IDs from
`formatRequirementId`, measurable targets, evidence level per the A–D rule, Kano class, assumptions,
uncertainties, conflicting findings), set the priority from the input port's ranking, and hand them
to `ctx.car.add`. Also export `answerChallenge(...)` for the API's challenge flow.
**Done when:** fixture records → filter → splitter → Add to Car runs fully offline with `mock`, all
outputs parse against the core schemas, and every finding's excerpt is verified.

### WS8 — Prioritization

**Owns:** `packages/blocks/src/prioritization/**`.
**Builds:** explainable scoring used by the AI Splitter's priority mode. Factors are computed
deterministically where possible: customer impact from mentions, sentiment and sales volume; evidence
strength from independent sources × reliability and evidence level; competitive gap from
`competitor_advantage` findings; trend momentum from `market_trend` findings. The LLM is used only
where a judgement is needed (brand fit, ease), always with a one-line note. It uses `weightedTotal`
and `priorityForScore` and writes a readable `priorityRationale` naming the top drivers. It also flags
"high score, weak evidence".
**Done when:** scores are reproducible for the fixtures, changing Settings weights changes the ranking as
expected (tested), and each factor has a note a PM can understand.

## What works right now (maintained by WS0)

- **App shell:** Electron desktop app with three tabs at the bottom, **Data Flow · Car · Settings**
  (⌘/Ctrl + 1–3), light and dark theme in the BMW M colorway. `npm run dev` to try it,
  `npm run smoke` to check it (drives the real app, screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`).

  HIL, Add to Car), drag or click onto the workplace, connect ports (invalid connections and loops are
  refused with a reason), inspector with placeholder parameters, splitter branches and Add to Car
  rankings become ports, Custom/Research/AI Filter open into inner workplaces (breadcrumb back),
  delete with confirmation. The flow lives in memory: **not saved yet** and **nothing runs yet**.

  collected (lineage across inner workplaces) and a table icon on every step to see the data there
  (a Raw step's own data, a HIL's connected Raw inputs, or the saved run; no demo data). Runtime logic (pause until reviewed, then pass on) is built and
  tested; it runs once the executor exists.
- **Raw block (built, WS5):** reads `.xlsx` (any sheet), CSV (`,` `;` tab, UTF-8 or Windows-1252, German
  number formats) and read-only SQLite queries into one source + one record per row, with
  deterministic usage findings from take rates and sales volumes. "Choose file…" opens the native

  data (`blocks.preview`). Synthetic samples in `data/samples/`. Also reads BMW's real exports

  `data/raw/`; the PDF option list is refused for now.
- **Car:** 3D car with every requirement from Add to Car placed on a part (WS3); **Reset** removes
  all requirements (audited, ids never reused). No demo data: the car is empty until a flow runs.
- **Settings:** App, Global parameters, AI & research, Collaboration, About. Changes are validated and
  apply live (theme, grid, minimap). **Not saved to disk yet** (`settings.save` is WS1).
- **Contract:** domain schemas, block specs (`core/src/blocks.ts`), graph rules (`core/src/graph.ts`),
  IPC API, scoring formula, synthetic F70 EU fixtures, block registry, default template.
  Built block implementations: Raw, HIL. **No executor or database exists yet**, so flows don't run.

  method answers `not_implemented`.

2: import { noopLogger, type IMastraLogger } from "@mastra/core/logger";
3: import type { LlmClient, LlmTextRequest, Settings } from "@reqflow/core";
4: import { z } from "zod";
5: import { cancellable, Request } from "./client-request";
6: import type { LlmClientOptions } from "./index";
7: 
8: /** Small request seam for offline tests; it does not expose tools, storage, or credentials discovery. */
9: export interface MastraAgentConfig {
10:   id: string;
11:   name: string;
12:   instructions: string;
13:   model: { providerId: "anthropic"; modelId: string; apiKey: string };
14:   maxRetries: 0;
15:   errorProcessorDefaults: false;
16: }
17: 
18: export interface MastraGenerateOptions {
19:   abortSignal?: AbortSignal;
20:   maxSteps: 1;
21:   modelSettings: { temperature: number; maxOutputTokens: number; maxRetries: 0 };
22:   structuredOutput?: {
23:     schema: z.ZodType<unknown>;
24:     errorStrategy: "strict";
25:     logger: IMastraLogger;
26:   };
27: }
28:

30:   object?: unknown;
31:   text?: string;
32:   finishReason?: string;
33:   response?: { modelId?: string };
34:   error?: unknown;
35:   usedFallbackValue?: boolean;
36: }
37: 
38: export interface MastraAgent {
39:   generate(prompt: string, options: MastraGenerateOptions): Promise<MastraGenerateResult>;
40: }
41: 
42: export type MastraAgentFactory = (config: MastraAgentConfig) => MastraAgent;
43: 
44: export interface MastraLlmClientOptions extends LlmClientOptions {
45:   /** Replaces only Agent construction/generation; production uses the standalone Mastra Agent. */
46:   createAgent?: MastraAgentFactory;
47: }
48: 
49: const createAgent: MastraAgentFactory = (config) => {
50:   // Do not attach a Mastra instance: no tracing, memory, storage, tools, or source logging.
51:   const agent = new Agent(config);
52:   agent.__setLogger(noopLogger);
53:   return {
54:     generate: (prompt, options) =>
55:       options.structuredOutput
56:         ? agent.generate(prompt, { ...options, structuredOutput: options.structuredOutput })
57:         : agent.generate(prompt, { ...options, structuredOutput: undefined }),
58:   };
59: };
60: 
61: /** Provider errors can contain request bodies and credentials; expose only a numeric HTTP status. */
62: function providerError(error: unknown): Error {
63:   let current = error;
64:   for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current && typeof current === "object"; depth++) {
65:     const { statusCode, cause } = current as { statusCode?: unknown; cause?: unknown };
66:     if (
67:       typeof statusCode === "number" &&
68:       Number.isInteger(statusCode) &&
69:       statusCode >= 400 &&
70:       statusCode <= 599
71:     ) {
72:       return new Error(`Mastra Anthropic request failed (HTTP ${statusCode})`);
73:     }
74:     current = cause;
75:   }
76:   return new Error(
77:     "Mastra Anthropic generation failed; check model configuration, connectivity, or provider response.",
78:   );
79: }
80: 
81: /** Internal Anthropic provider; the public factory validates settings and reuses the existing mock. */
82: export function createMastraProvider(
83:   config: Settings["llm"],
84:   options: MastraLlmClientOptions,
85: ): LlmClient {
86:   const apiKey = options.apiKey?.trim();
87:   if (!apiKey) throw new Error("Anthropic API key is required; supply it from the secret store.");
88:   // Mastra's model router has no fetch option. Never silently ignore a caller's test transport.
89:   if (options.fetch && !options.createAgent) {
90:     throw new Error(
91:       "Inject createAgent for offline Mastra tests; use createLlmClient for fetch overrides.",
92:     );
93:   }
94:   const factory = options.createAgent ?? createAgent;
95: 
96:   async function generate(request: LlmTextRequest, schema?: z.ZodType<unknown>) {
97:     request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
98:     const checked = Request.parse(request);
99:     let result: MastraGenerateResult;
100:     try {
101:       result = await cancellable(() => {
102:         const agent = factory({
103:           id: "reqflow-llm",
104:           name: "ReqFlow LLM",
105:           instructions: checked.system ?? "",
106:           model: {
107:             providerId: "anthropic",
108:             modelId: checked.tier === "fast" ? config.fastModel : config.model,
109:             apiKey: apiKey!,
110:           },
111:           maxRetries: 0,
112:           // Mastra stability processors otherwise retry independently of model maxRetries.
113:           errorProcessorDefaults: false,
114:         });
115:         return agent.generate(checked.prompt, {
116:           abortSignal: request.signal,
117:           maxSteps: 1,
118:           modelSettings: { temperature: config.temperature, maxOutputTokens: 8192, maxRetries: 0 },
119:           ...(schema
120:             ? { structuredOutput: { schema, errorStrategy: "strict" as const, logger: noopLogger } }
121:             : {}),
122:         });
123:       }, request.signal);
124:       if (result.error) throw result.error;
125:     } catch (error) {
126:       request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
127:       throw providerError(error);
128:     }
129:     if (result.finishReason !== "stop" || result.usedFallbackValue) {
130:       throw new Error(
131:         "Mastra Anthropic response is incomplete, refused, or substituted; no output was accepted.",
132:       );
133:     }
134:     const model = z.string().min(1).parse(result.response?.modelId);
135:     return { result, model };
136:   }
137: 
138:   return {
139:     async generateObject(request) {
140:       const { result, model } = await generate(request, request.schema);
141:       if (result.object === undefined)
142:         throw new Error("Mastra Anthropic structured response is missing its object.");
143:       // Mastra validation is not a substitute for the caller's original Zod refinements.
144:       const object = request.schema.parse(result.object);
145:       request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
146:       return { object, model };
147:     },
148:     async generateText(request) {
149:       const { result, model } = await generate(request);
150:       const text = z.string().min(1).parse(result.text);
151:       request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
152:       return { text, model };
153:     },
154:   };
155: }

1: import {
2:   DATA_KEYS,
3:   Finding,
4:   PipelineData,
5:   Requirement,
6:   Source,
7:   SourceRecord,
8:   Theme,
9:   type DataKey,
10:   type StoredFile,
11: } from "@reqflow/core";
12: 
13: const MAX_JSON_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
14: const schemas = {
15:   sources: Source,
16:   records: SourceRecord,
17:   findings: Finding,
18:   themes: Theme,
19:   requirements: Requirement,
20: };
21: 
22: /** Detect only declared JSON files; do not guess an envelope from CSV or spreadsheet contents. */
23: export function isResearchJsonFile(file: Pick<StoredFile, "name" | "mimeType">): boolean {
24:   const mime = file.mimeType.split(";", 1)[0]!.trim().toLowerCase();
25:   return /\.json$/i.test(file.name) || /^(application|text)\/(?:json|[^/\s]+\+json)$/.test(mime);
26: }
27: 
28: function fail(path: string, reason: string): never {
29:   // Paths and reasons are constructed here, never from data values or native parser messages.
30:   throw new Error(`Research JSON: ${path} ${reason}`);
31: }
32: 
33: function indexById<T extends { id: string }>(items: T[], layer: DataKey): Map<string, T> {
34:   const byId = new Map<string, T>();
35:   for (const [index, item] of items.entries()) {
36:     if (byId.has(item.id)) fail(`${layer}[${index}].id`, "is a duplicate ID.");
37:     byId.set(item.id, item);
38:   }
39:   return byId;
40: }
41: 
42: /** Only explicit scalar IDs count; never infer an identity from arbitrary fields or wording. */
43: function identityField(record: SourceRecord, names: string[]): string | undefined {
44:   const fields = Object.entries(record.fields ?? {});
45:   for (const name of names) {
46:     for (const [key, value] of fields) {
47:       if (key.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, "") !== name.toLowerCase()) continue;
48:       if (typeof value === "string" && value.trim()) return value;
49:       if (typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value)) return String(value);
50:     }
51:   }
52:   return undefined;
53: }
54: 
55: function checkIdentities(data: PipelineData): void {
56:   // A web URI identifies a document. Internal sources may share an upload URI across sheets.
57:   // No URL normalization is applied: queries and fragments can identify different evidence.
58:   const sourceUris = new Set<string>();
59:   for (const [index, source] of data.sources.entries()) {
60:     const uri = source.uri?.trim();
61:     if (source.origin !== "web" || !uri) continue;
62:     if (sourceUris.has(uri)) fail(`sources[${index}].uri`, "is a duplicate web source identity.");
63:     sourceUris.add(uri);
64:   }
65: 
66:   // Only an explicit original/comment ID in fields verifies a repeated entry. Scope it to the
67:   // source, provider and customer: local comment IDs may repeat across providers or customers.
68:   // Text and locators do not identify people or comments. Without an explicit original ID,
69:   // distinct core record IDs remain independent, even with identical text and locators.
70:   const recordIdentities = new Set<string>();
71:   for (const [index, record] of data.records.entries()) {
72:     const original = identityField(record, [
73:       "originalId",
74:       "originalRecordId",
75:       "originalCommentId",
76:       "providerRecordId",
77:       "reviewId",
78:       "feedbackId",
79:       "responseId",
80:       "commentId",
81:     ]);
82:     if (original === undefined) continue;
83:     const identity = JSON.stringify([
84:       record.sourceId,
85:       identityField(record, ["provider", "providerId", "providerName"]) ?? null,
86:       original,
87:       identityField(record, ["customerId", "respondentId", "authorId", "userId"]) ?? null,
88:     ]);
89:     if (recordIdentities.has(identity))
90:       fail(`records[${index}]`, "is a duplicate record identity.");
91:     recordIdentities.add(identity);
92:   }
93: }
94: 
95: function checkReferences(data: PipelineData): void {
96:   const sources = indexById(data.sources, "sources");
97:   const records = indexById(data.records, "records");
98:   const findings = indexById(data.findings, "findings");
99:   const themes = indexById(data.themes, "themes");
100:   indexById(data.requirements, "requirements");
101:   checkIdentities(data);
102: 
103:   const requireReference = (exists: boolean, path: string, layer: DataKey) => {
104:     if (!exists) fail(path, `must reference an item in ${layer}.`);
105:   };
106:   for (const [index, record] of data.records.entries()) {
107:     requireReference(sources.has(record.sourceId), `records[${index}].sourceId`, "sources");
108:   }
109:   for (const [index, finding] of data.findings.entries()) {
110:     if (finding.themeId !== undefined) {
111:       requireReference(themes.has(finding.themeId), `findings[${index}].themeId`, "themes");
112:     }
113:     for (const [evidenceIndex, evidence] of finding.evidence.entries()) {
114:       const path = `findings[${index}].evidence[${evidenceIndex}]`;
115:       requireReference(sources.has(evidence.sourceId), `${path}.sourceId`, "sources");
116:       if (evidence.recordId === undefined) continue; // Source-only evidence is allowed by core.
117:       const record = records.get(evidence.recordId);
118:       requireReference(record !== undefined, `${path}.recordId`, "records");
119:       if (record!.sourceId !== evidence.sourceId) {
120:         fail(`${path}.sourceId`, "does not match the linked record's source.");
121:       }
122:       if (!record!.text.includes(evidence.excerpt)) {
123:         fail(`${path}.excerpt`, "must be verbatim text from the linked record.");
124:       }
125:     }
126:   }
127:   for (const [index, theme] of data.themes.entries()) {
128:     for (const [linkIndex, id] of theme.findingIds.entries()) {
129:       requireReference(findings.has(id), `themes[${index}].findingIds[${linkIndex}]`, "findings");
130:     }
131:   }
132:   for (const [index, requirement] of data.requirements.entries()) {
133:     for (const field of ["findingIds", "conflictingFindingIds"] as const) {
134:       for (const [linkIndex, id] of requirement[field].entries()) {
135:         requireReference(
136:           findings.has(id),
137:           `requirements[${index}].${field}[${linkIndex}]`,
138:           "findings",
139:         );
140:       }
141:     }
142:     for (const [linkIndex, id] of requirement.sourceIds.entries()) {
143:       requireReference(
144:         sources.has(id),
145:         `requirements[${index}].sourceIds[${linkIndex}]`,
146:         "sources",
147:       );
148:     }
149:   }
150: }
151: 
152: /**
153:  * Accept a core PipelineData envelope or a structural Research dataset with sources and records.
154:  * Only absent findings/themes/requirements default to []; malformed supplied layers are errors.
155:  * Core schemas validate every layer, but their stripped parse output is deliberately discarded:
156:  * original objects, nested extensions, provenance and envelope metadata must survive unchanged.
157:  * Duplicate IDs/identities and dangling references fail instead of silently dropping evidence.
158:  * Errors contain only trusted schema fields and array indexes, never file contents or causes.
159:  */
160: export function parseResearchJson(bytes: Uint8Array): PipelineData & Record<string, unknown> {
161:   if (bytes.byteLength > MAX_JSON_BYTES) {
162:     throw new Error("Research JSON exceeds the 16 MiB file limit.");
163:   }
164:   let input: unknown;
165:   try {
166:     input = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true }).decode(bytes));
167:   } catch {
168:     throw new Error("Research JSON must contain valid UTF-8 JSON.");
169:   }
170:   if (
171:     !input ||
172:     typeof input !== "object" ||
173:     Array.isArray(input) ||
174:     !("sources" in input) ||
175:     !Array.isArray(input.sources) ||
176:     !("records" in input) ||
177:     !Array.isArray(input.records)
178:   ) {
179:     throw new Error("Research JSON must be an object with sources and records arrays.");
180:   }
181:   const data = { findings: [], themes: [], requirements: [], ...input };
182:   const validated = PipelineData.safeParse(data);
183:   if (!validated.success) {
184:     const issue = validated.error.issues[0]!;
185:     const layer = DATA_KEYS.find((key) => key === issue.path[0]);
186:     let path: string = layer ?? "envelope";
187:     if (layer && typeof issue.path[1] === "number") {
188:       path += `[${issue.path[1]}]`;
189:       const field = issue.path[2];
190:       if (typeof field === "string" && Object.hasOwn(schemas[layer].shape, field)) {
191:         path += `.${field}`;
192:       }
193:     }
194:     fail(path, `does not match the core schema (${issue.code}).`);
195:   }
196:   const original = data as PipelineData & Record<string, unknown>;
197:   checkReferences(original);
198:   return original;
199: }

+## AI Splitter: raw analysis and review

+The raw-data splitter uses a standalone Mastra `Agent` behind the existing injected `LlmClient`.
+It receives the run's model configuration and secret-store API key; the Agent is not attached to a
+Mastra instance, tools, storage, memory or tracing. Structured requests use strict Zod validation,
+one generation step and no retries. Tests can inject the Agent factory, while production defaults
+to the standalone implementation. Legacy `priority`, `category`, `sentiment` and `custom` routing
+modes remain available alongside raw-data `customer_priority`, `car_parts` and `custom` analysis.

+then assigns against the consolidated catalog. Car-part/custom modes create exactly the configured
+2–10 global groups before assignment; customer-priority mode uses canonical needs and creates 2–10
+demand bands. Oversized prompts fail explicitly rather than truncating evidence. Code verifies
+complete item/need coverage and each cited source, record, locator and verbatim excerpt. The model
+does not return scores, unit IDs, routes or human decisions.

+customer count is unknown. Explicit original/provider identities and reimport evidence can deduplicate
+units, while distinct record/customer identities remain independent even if their text matches.

+weighted 70%; mean explicitly expressed supporting impact is weighted 30%. An absent impact anchor is

+unclear evidence remains visible, and confidence is not demand. Output retains a versioned analytical
+report with score method, group scores, item assignments, evidence, source matrix, limitations and
+human review history. The report is stored with the `BlockRun` snapshot and rendered as score,
+evidence-balance and source-by-group graphics with exact evidence drill-down.
+
+At a paused eligible HIL, a reviewer may correct individual item routes with a required rationale.
+Corrections update the run's routing report and audit history; computed scores and original evidence
+remain unchanged. The review is available only while the upstream splitter is behind the current
+paused HIL with reviewer edits enabled. It never edits or decides a requirement; requirement
+approval, rejection or deferral remains a separate human action on the Car page.
